questions.q: What is the main advantage of a small chunk size?
options: It always eliminates the need for chunk overlap
It retrieves with high precision — if it matches a query, it's very likely genuinely relevant
It removes the need for an embedding model
It guarantees the chunk never needs metadata
questions.explain: A small chunk has little room to contain unrelated content, so a match on it is very likely to be genuinely about the query — at the cost of missing surrounding context.

questions.q: What is the main risk of a large chunk size?
options: It becomes impossible to embed
It cannot be stored in a vector database
It often mixes several topics, so one relevant sentence can drag an otherwise-irrelevant chunk into the results
It always produces a lower embedding dimensionality
questions.explain: A large chunk is more likely to contain multiple unrelated topics, which reduces retrieval precision even when it carries more surrounding context.

questions.q: What is the 'lost in the middle' problem referenced in this lesson?
options: Vector databases lose points that are stored in the middle of an index
Relevant content placed in the middle of a long prompt tends to get used less reliably than content near the start or end
Chunks in the middle of a document are skipped during ingestion
The middle of a chunk is always truncated by the embedding model
questions.explain: Research on long-context models has found that information in the middle of a long prompt is used less reliably than information near the edges — a risk when stuffing many large chunks into one prompt.

questions.q: According to this lesson's starting ranges, which use case is suggested to use the largest chunk size?
options: FAQ and support tickets
Social media posts
Technical documentation
Contracts and long-form reports
questions.explain: Contracts and long-form reports are suggested at 500-800 tokens, since clauses and findings often depend on nearby context that a smaller chunk would cut off.

questions.q: Why does this lesson say chunk size and top_k should be tuned together?
options: Because top_k has no effect on retrieval quality
Because smaller chunks usually need a higher top_k to assemble enough context, while larger chunks usually need a lower top_k
Because top_k only applies when chunk overlap is zero
Because chunk size and top_k must always be set to the same numeric value
questions.explain: Since each small chunk carries less context on its own, more of them are usually needed per query (higher top_k); larger chunks already carry more context and are costlier to stuff many of into one prompt, so a lower top_k usually fits better.
